q: 1. In a closed traverse the algebraic sum of deflection angle is ...............
explain: For a closed traverse, the algebraic sum of the deflection angles must equal 360°.

q: 2. In a precision traverse, included angles are measured by setting the vernier ...............
options: to read zero exactly on back station
to read 5° exactly on back station
somewhere near zero and reading both verniers on back station
explain: In high-precision work, instead of setting to exactly zero, it's better to read the actual initial readings on both verniers to eliminate setting errors.

q: 3. Which of the following error is not eliminated by the method of repetition of horizontal angle measurement?
options: Error due to eccentricity of verniers
Error due to displacement of station signals
Error due to wrong adjustment of line of collimation and trunnion axis
explain: If the station signal itself has moved or is displaced, repeating the angle measurement from the same (wrong) signal location will not fix the error.

q: 4. Closed traverse is suitable in the survey of
explain: A closed traverse, which returns to its starting point, is suitable for surveying areas that form a closed loop, like the boundary of a pond/lake; rivers, roads and coastlines are elongated features better surveyed by open traverses.

q: 5. The distance between terminal points computed from a subsidiary traverse run between them, is generally known as
explain: When a subsidiary (auxiliary) traverse is run between two points to establish the distance between them, the computed distance is called the traverse base.

q: 6. The included angles of a theodolite traverse, are generally measured
explain: Included angles in a theodolite traverse are conventionally measured clockwise, starting the observation from the back (previous) station and swinging to the forward station.

q: 7. Under ordinary conditions, the precision of a theodolite traverse is affected by
explain: Under normal conditions, angular measurements with a theodolite are quite precise and accidental errors in angle are small; it is the systematic (cumulative) errors in the linear (chain/tape) measurements that mainly govern the overall precision of the traverse.

q: 8. The most reliable method of plotting a theodolite traverse is
options: by consecutive co-ordinates of each station
by independent co-ordinates of each station
by plotting included angles and scaling off each traverse leg
by the tangent method of plotting
explain: Plotting by independent (total) co-ordinates of each station, computed from the origin, avoids the accumulation of plotting errors that occurs when each point is plotted relative to the previous one (consecutive co-ordinates), making it the most reliable method.

q: 9. The latitude of a traverse leg is obtained by multiplying its length by
explain: Latitude (the north-south component) of a traverse leg = Length x cosine(reduced bearing), since latitude is the projection of the line onto the north-south axis.

q: 10. In a closed traverse, sum of south latitudes exceeds the sum of north latitudes and the sum of east departures exceeds the sum of west departures, then, the closing line will lie in
explain: The closing error (line needed to close the traverse) runs opposite to the net imbalance; since the traverse itself trends south and east, the closing line to bring it back runs north and west, i.e. lies in the north-west quadrant.

q: 11. The operation of making the algebraic sum of latitudes and departures of a closed traverse, each equal to zero, is known
explain: Adjusting all the latitudes and departures of a closed traverse so that their algebraic sums each become zero (removing the closing error) is called balancing the traverse.

q: 12. If the angular measurements of a traverse are more precise than its linear measurements, balancing of the traverse, is done by
explain: The Transit rule is used to balance a traverse when angular measurements are considered more precise/reliable than the linear measurements, since it corrects latitudes and departures independently in proportion to their own magnitudes rather than the total leg length.

q: 13. A well conditioned triangle has no angle less than ...............
explain: A triangle is well-conditioned if its angles are between 30° and 120° to ensure accurate intersection points.

q: 14. In a closed traverse
options: the difference between fore bearing & back bearing should be 90°
the sum of included angles should be (2N-4) right angle, where N is the number of sides
the sum of inclined angles should be (2N-1), where N is the number of sides
explain: The geometric property of a closed polygon dictates that the sum of the interior angles is given by the formula (2N - 4) x 90 degrees.

q: 15. An axis about which the telescope can be rotated in a horizontal plane is called
explain: Rotation in a horizontal plane happens around the vertical axis. Rotation in a vertical plane happens around the horizontal (trunnion) axis.

q: 16. In a theodolite the line of collimation is
options: parallel to axes of plate level
explain: For correct instrument geometry, the line of collimation of a theodolite telescope must be exactly perpendicular to the trunnion (horizontal) axis about which the telescope rotates.

q: 17. Axis of altitude level is
options: parallel to the line of collimation
explain: The altitude level (attached to the telescope) has its axis parallel to the line of collimation of the telescope, so it can be used to check/set the line of sight horizontal even when the telescope's own bubble is out of adjustment.

q: 18. A 15 cm theodolite means
options: length of the telescope is 15 cm
diameter of lower plate is 15 cm
radius of upper plate is 15 cm.
explain: The size of a theodolite is designated by the diameter of its lower (graduated horizontal) plate; thus a '15 cm theodolite' has a lower plate 15 cm in diameter.

q: 19. In precision theodolite traverse... the angular error of closure should not exceed
explain: For standard/ordinary traversing, the error is often capped at $1' \sqrt{N}$, where N is the number of stations.

q: 20. The most commonly used set of theodolite operations are
explain: The standard convention for taking a 'set' of theodolite observations is to start with the face-left position swinging right (clockwise), then observe face-right swinging left.

q: 21. The projection of a traverse line on a line perpendicular to the meridian is known as
explain: Departure is the projection of a line on the East-West axis (perpendicular to the North-South meridian).

q: 22. left swing is not much favoured in theodolite survey because
options: most of the surveyors are accustomed to right hand
it is inconvenient to turn the telescope anti-clockwise
vertical scale comes to an inconvenient position to be read.
explain: Since the horizontal circle of a theodolite is graduated to increase in the clockwise direction, swinging the telescope anti-clockwise (left swing) causes the readings to decrease, which is inconvenient for booking and computation.

q: 23. The projection of a traverse line on a line parallel to the meridian is known as
explain: Latitude is the projection of a line on the North-South axis (parallel to the meridian).

q: 24. In a closed traverse the algebraic sum of deflection angle is
explain: For a closed traverse, the algebraic sum of all the deflection angles (right deflections positive, left negative) is always equal to 360 degrees.

q: 25. When internal angles are to be subtended by a theodolite survey for closed traverse
options: exterior angles are measured when the traverse goes anti-clockwise.
explain: To measure the internal (interior) angles of a closed traverse correctly and consistently, the traverse should be run in the counter-clockwise direction.

q: 26. When the first object is to be focused, the scale, is set to 0 deg 00'00" and then
options: the upper screw is fixed , lower screw released, the object sighted, lower screw fixed and lower tangent screw operated
both the clamp screw fixed, to tangent screw operated
bottom clamp screw fixed, top screw released, the object sighted and upper tangent screw operated
object is exactly bisected by operating both the upper and lower tangent screws whichever is convenient.
explain: The standard procedure to set an initial zero reading is: fix the upper clamp, release the lower clamp, roughly sight the object, then fix the lower clamp and use the lower tangent screw to bisect the object exactly.

q: 27. The process of turning the telescope about the vertical axis in horizontal plane is known as
explain: Swinging is the rotation of the theodolite telescope in a horizontal plane. Turning it in a vertical plane is called transiting or plunging.

q: 28. For which of the following permanent adjustments of theodolite, the spire test is used?
options: adjustment of altitude bubble and vertical index frame
explain: The spire test is used to make the horizontal axis perpendicular to the vertical axis.

q: 29. A traverse survey can be plotted
options: by rectangular coordinates or plotting by tangents
by paper protractor or by included angles
by parallel meridian method or plotting by chords
explain: All the mentioned methods are valid ways to transfer field traverse data onto paper.

q: 30. Traversing is generally done by
explain: A traverse survey can be carried out using a chain (chain traversing), a compass, a theodolite, or a plane table, depending on the accuracy required, so all methods are applicable.

q: 31. The angular error of closure or summation error should not exceed
options: 3√N where N is number of stations or sides.
explain: The standard permissible angular closure error in compass surveying is typically defined as 15' multiplied by the square root of the number of stations.

q: 32. If 'n' is the number of sides, then the total sum of interior angles of a closed traverse should be
explain: The sum of interior angles of a closed polygon of n sides is given by the standard geometric formula (2n - 4) x 90 degrees.

q: 33. If 'n' is the number of sides, then the total sum of exterior angles of a closed traverse should be
explain: Since interior and exterior angles at each vertex are supplementary and their total for all n vertices is 4 right angles more than the interior sum, the sum of exterior angles works out to (2n + 4) x 90 degrees.

q: 34. In order to measure a horizontal angle more accurately than a vernier, a
options: method of deflection angles is used
method of double observations is used
explain: The method of repetition involves measuring the same angle multiple times and dividing the total by the number of repetitions, which reduces the error caused by the least count of the vernier.

q: 35. In measuring horizontal angles, the theodolite should be turned
options: clockwise from the forward station to the back station
clockwise from the back station to the forward station
anticlockwise from the back station to the forward station
anticlockwise from the forward station to the back station
explain: Standard practice for measuring horizontal angles with a theodolite is to sight the back station, set the scale, and then turn the instrument clockwise to the forward station.

q: 36. According to Bowditch Rule, the correction to latitude (or departure) of any side is equal to
options: Length of the side / Perimeter of traverse
Perimeter of traverse / Length of the side
Total error in latitude / Perimeter of traverse
Total error in latitude x Length of that side / Perimeter of traverse
explain: Bowditch's rule states that the correction to the latitude (or departure) of a side is proportional to the length of that side: Correction = Total error in latitude x (Length of that side / Perimeter of traverse).

q: 37. Which of the following methods of theodolite traversing is suitable for locating the details which are far away from transit stations?
options: by measuring angle to the point from at least three stations
by measuring angles to the point from at least two stations
by measuring angel at one station and distance from other
by measuring distance from two points on traverse line
explain: Distant details, which cannot be directly chained, are located by the method of intersection, measuring angles to the point from at least two known theodolite stations.

q: 38. The theodolite is an instrument used for measuring very accurately .............
explain: The primary function of a theodolite is the precise measurement of both horizontal and vertical angles.

q: 39. The process of turning the telescope of a theodolite over its supporting axis through 180° in a vertical plane, is called .............
explain: Transiting, plunging, and reversing are synonymous terms for rotating the telescope 180° around its horizontal (trunnion) axis.

q: 40. An angle measured clockwise from the proceeding survey line to the following survey line is called
explain: A deflection angle is measured from the prolongation of the preceding line to the following line, and when the direction is clockwise, it is a right deflection angle.

q: 41. In precision theodolite traverse for roads and railways, the angular error of closure should not exceed
explain: For a precision theodolite traverse suitable for roads and railways, the permissible angular error of closure is 1 minute multiplied by the square root of the number of stations (N).

q: 42. For which of the following permanent adjustments of theodolite, the spire test is used?
explain: The spire test is specifically used to check and adjust the horizontal (trunnion) axis of a theodolite, ensuring it is truly horizontal by sighting a high point from both faces.

q: 43. In any closed traverse, if they survey work is correct, then .............
options: the algebraic sum of latitudes should be equal to zero
the algebraic sum of departures should be equal to zero
the sum of northings should be equal to the sum of southings
explain: For a closed traverse, the sum of latitudes (Northings - Southings) and departures (Eastings - Westings) must both equal zero.

q: 44. An angle between the inclined line of sight and the horizontal is called .............
explain: A vertical angle is the angle measured in the vertical plane between the line of sight and the horizontal line.

q: 45. In locating the details of inaccessible objects visible at least from transit stations, the method used is .............
options: by angles and distances from the same station
by angle from one station and distance from the other station
by distances from two different stations
explain: Inaccessible objects are often located by observing angles from known stations (intersection method).

q: 46. The traversing by the method of deflection angles is chiefly used in .............
explain: Deflection angle traversing is standard for 'open' traverses like roads, railways, and canals where the route continues forward.

q: 47. The angle between the prolongation of the preceding line and the forward line of a traverse is called
explain: As defined earlier (Q210), this angle between the prolongation of the preceding survey line and the following line is the deflection angle.

q: 48. In a theodolite the line of collimation is .............
options: parallel to axis of plate levels
explain: For a properly adjusted theodolite, the line of collimation (the optical axis) must be perpendicular to the horizontal (trunnion) axis.

q: 49. In a transit theodolite error due to eccentricity of verniers is counteracted by .............
options: reading different parts of main scale
taking both right swing and left swing reading
explain: Reading both verniers (A and B) and taking the mean value eliminates the error caused by the centers of the graduated circle and the alidade not coinciding.

q: 50. Right face and left reading are taken to .............
options: eliminate error of trunnion axis not exactly horizontal
eliminate error in the line of collimation
explain: Changing the face of the theodolite (Face Left and Face Right) eliminates errors due to the line of collimation not being perpendicular to the trunnion axis and the trunnion axis not being perpendicular to the vertical axis.
